content.content: Your task is to implement and verify the circular enqueue (push) operation for the Ring Buffer data structure. Unlike a standard queue which may have an infinite logical capacity or fail when full, this ring buffer is modeled as a fixed-capacity sequence that supports overwriting. Standard Case (Not Full): Verify that if the buffer has remaining capacity, the element is added to the "back" of the sequence, increasing the sequence length by one, while preserving the order of existing elements. Overwrite Case (Full): Verify that if the buffer is at maximum capacity, the operation remains successful by discarding the oldest element (the "front" at index 0). You must prove that the new model sequence consists of the original elements from indices 1 through $N-1$, with the new element appended at the end, maintaining the fixed capacity. ---- 1 use vstd::prelude::*; 2 3 verus! { 4 // Following is the block for necessary definitions 5 // 6 // A RingBuffer wrapper around a Vec 7 struct RingBuffer { 8 pub data: Vec, 9 pub head: usize, 10 pub len: usize, 11 pub capacity: usize, 12 } 13 14 impl RingBuffer { 15 pub open spec fn view(&self) -> Seq { 16 Seq::new(self.len as nat, |i: int| 17 self.data.view()[(self.head as int + i) % self.capacity as int] 18 ) 19 } 20 21 pub open spec fn is_valid(&self) -> bool { 22 &&& self.capacity > 0 23 &&& self.data.view().len() == self.capacity as nat 24 &&& self.len <= self.capacity 25 &&& self.head < self.capacity 26 } 27 28 pub fn new(capacity: usize, fill_value: T) -> (s: Self) 29 requires capacity > 0 30 ensures 31 s.is_valid(), 32 s.view().len() == 0, 33 s.capacity == capacity, 34 { 35 let mut data = Vec::with_capacity(capacity); 36 let mut i = 0; 37 while i < capacity 38 invariant 39 data.view().len() == i as nat, 40 i <= capacity, 41 { 42 data.push(fill_value); 43 i = i + 1; 44 } 45 RingBuffer { data, head: 0, len: 0, capacity } 46 } 47 // 48 49 // Following is the block for potential helper specifications 50 // 51 52 // 53 54 // Following is the block for proofs of lemmas, or functions that help the implementation or verification of the main specification 55 // 56 57 // 58 59 // Following is the block for the main specification 60 // 61 // Enqueue with Overwrite 62 pub fn enqueue(&mut self, value: T) 63 requires 64 old(self).is_valid(), 65 ensures 66 self.is_valid(), 67 self.capacity == old(self).capacity, 68 // Case 1: If it wasn't full, it's like a normal push 69 old(self).len < old(self).capacity ==> 70 self.view() == old(self).view().push(value), 71 // Case 2: If it was full, we drop the first (oldest) and then push 72 old(self).len == old(self).capacity ==> 73 self.view() == old(self).view().drop_first().push(value), 74 // 75 // 76 { 77 78 } 79 // 80 } 81 82 fn main() {} 83 84 }description.md ringbuffer_enqueue.rs

DONE <- `verus /work/ringbuffer_enqueue.rs` prints `verification results:: 10 verified, 0 errors` with no errors.

The enqueue is implemented in `/work/ringbuffer_enqueue.rs`, and the two postconditions (not-full append and full overwrite) are proven.

**Approach**
- **Not full (`len < cap`):** write `value` at physical index `(head + len) % cap` and increment `len`. The index is computed without overflow as `head - (cap - len)` or `head + len`.
- **Full (`len == cap`):** overwrite the slot at `head`, then advance `head` to `(head + 1) % cap`. `len` stays at `cap`.
- **Helpers** (in the `<helpers>` block): `lemma_mod_shift` (mod distributes over an offset), `lemma_mod_inj` (distinct offsets below `cap` give distinct slots), `lemma_idx` (the branch index equals `(head+len)%cap`), and `lemma_head_next` (the new head equals `(head+1)%cap`).
- **Proofs:** the not-full case uses `assert_seqs_equal!` with the helpers. The full case uses an explicit `assert forall` over indices `0..cap`, split into the last index (which reads the overwritten slot) and the rest (which read old index `i+1`).

**Edits**
- Changes are confined to the `<helpers>`, `<code>` and `<proofs>` blocks (the proofs block is empty). All marker comments are kept.
- The preamble, `use` lines, signature, `requires`/`ensures`, and `fn main` are unchanged.
- No `assume`, `admit`, `unsafe`, `extern`, `external_body`, or other trust attributes are used.
- There are no recursive functions and no `while` or `loop`.
- Scratch files I created are removed; only the two original files remain in `/work`.
